factual_and_methodological.summary: NDB primary sources confirm ten member countries after Uzbekistan's June 5, 2026 accession, 19 projects and US$3.171bn approved in 2025, a 115-project / US$35.593bn approved portfolio at year-end, and Board of Governors approval of the 2027-2031 strategy in September 2026. The dossier distinguishes treaty-based bank governance from informal BRICS political coordination and separates approvals from realised assets.

editorial_publication_readiness.opening: Direct mechanism-led opening; no generic sophistication claims or product-process narration.
editorial_publication_readiness.headings: Headings advance the actor-specific mechanism, constraints, contrary evidence and revision conditions.
editorial_publication_readiness.language_localization: EN and PT-BR are semantically aligned; PT-BR technical prose was localized before approval.
editorial_publication_readiness.cohesion: Argument moves from rights/capability through transmission, constraints and evidence that would revise the assessment.
editorial_publication_readiness.template_meta_qa: No prompt, QA-process, schema, renderer or roadmap leakage detected.

contextual_depth.summary: The dossier distinguishes legal rights, operating capability, transmission, substitutability and institutional constraints rather than relying on scale or reputation.

visual_evidence_readiness.signature: At least two analytical tables, one quantitative chart, one causal flow and one mind map in both locales.
visual_evidence_readiness.limitations: Visuals encode sourced quantities or mechanisms defended in prose and are not combined into a synthetic power score.

contrary_evidence: Borrowers can access domestic, bilateral, private and other multilateral sources, so NDB relevance depends on whether its terms add financing capacity rather than merely replace another lender.
Approved projects may be delayed, partially disbursed or underperform after completion.
limitations: The 2027-2031 strategy is an approved future operating framework, not evidence of realised outcomes.
Local-currency finance reduces some FX mismatch only where funding depth and pricing make it viable; it does not remove construction or credit risk.
notes: Dedicated single-actor Strategic Actors dossier. Primary-source factual core, controlled taxonomy, bilingual parity and visual evidence reviewed; no public bundle for this ID at approval time.

en.title: New Development Bank: multilateral development finance beyond the founding BRICS membership
en.deck: The NDB has expanded from five founding BRICS members to ten member countries while building a distinct infrastructure-finance platform. Its structural relevance depends on converting member capital and market funding into additional, well-performing projects.
en.regime: The NDB is broadening membership and moving into a 2027–2031 strategy while maintaining treaty-based governance and development-finance operations.
en.key_risk: Treating the NDB as a single geopolitical instrument for BRICS members obscures its separate governance, project-level underwriting and the distinction between approvals and realised assets.

pt-BR.title: New Development Bank: financiamento multilateral do desenvolvimento além dos membros fundadores do BRICS
pt-BR.deck: O NDB passou dos cinco fundadores do BRICS para dez países membros enquanto constrói uma plataforma própria de financiamento de infraestrutura. Sua relevância depende de converter capital dos membros e funding de mercado em projetos adicionais e de bom desempenho.
pt-BR.regime: O NDB amplia sua base de membros e entra na estratégia 2027–2031 mantendo governança de tratado e operações de financiamento do desenvolvimento.
pt-BR.key_risk: Tratar o NDB como instrumento geopolítico único dos membros do BRICS esconde sua governança própria, análise de projetos e diferença entre aprovação e ativo realizado.
